tasks.title: Stripping end-to-end verifier tests incl. GoTo survival (AC-B2 + CLI round-trip)
tasks.description: Create tests/test_stripping_profiles.cpp that optimizes the four stripping corpus PDFs under each profile via the optimizer API and asserts the per-profile removal matrix, non-JS /OpenAction GoTo survival, /AA removal under JS-strip, and explicit CLI-flag-wins round-trip. Verification only: if any test exposes a strip-logic gap, record it and stop, do not change strip semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given the four stripping corpus PDFs (with_form, with_bookmarks_and_links, with_javascript, with_metadata) with real dict keys, when optimized with forProfile(MaxQuality), then 0 items are removed on all four (all *Removed counts 0, metadataStripped false).

Given the same four PDFs, when optimized with forProfile(Balanced), then jsRemoved>=1 on with_javascript.pdf and metadataStripped==true on with_metadata.pdf and nothing else, where "nothing else" scopes to the six removal counters only (linksRemoved/annotationsRemoved/bookmarksRemoved/formsRemoved/jsRemoved-on-non-JS-files/namedDestinationsRemoved ==0 on files lacking those elements); metadataStripped is NOT asserted on metadata-free PDFs (Balanced applies stripMetadata=true, which reports true on all inputs per the ESC-008 intent ruling locked 2026-10-07).
Given the same four PDFs, when optimized with forProfile(MaxCompression), then >=1 item is removed on each of the four PDFs.

Given a PDF whose /OpenAction is a non-JS GoTo destination (staged in $TMPDIR, never committed), when optimized under every profile, then the GoTo /OpenAction survives in the output; and given /AA keys present, when optimized with stripJavaScript=true, then /AA is removed with jsRemoved>=1.

Given --profile balanced plus an explicit --strip-bookmarks override round-tripped through run_optimize CLI parsing semantics (forProfile then explicit flag wins), when optimized, then bookmarks are removed and the result breakdown logs the removal (explicit flag wins over profile default).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the four stripping corpus PDFs (with_form, with_bookmarks_and_links, with_javascript, with_metadata) with real dict keys, when optimized with forProfile(MaxQuality), then 0 items are removed on all four (all *Removed counts 0, metadataStripped false).
tests.description: Optimize each of the four corpus PDFs with forProfile(MaxQuality); assert all removal counters 0 and metadataStripped false; verify outputs pass QPDF().processFile.
tests.expected_result: All four MaxQuality runs succeed with zero removals.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the same four PDFs, when optimized with forProfile(Balanced), then jsRemoved>=1 on with_javascript.pdf and metadataStripped==true on with_metadata.pdf and nothing else, where "nothing else" scopes to the six removal counters only (linksRemoved/annotationsRemoved/bookmarksRemoved/formsRemoved/jsRemoved-on-non-JS-files/namedDestinationsRemoved ==0 on files lacking those elements); metadataStripped is NOT asserted on metadata-free PDFs (Balanced applies stripMetadata=true, which reports true on all inputs per the ESC-008 intent ruling locked 2026-10-07).
tests.description: Optimize each of the four corpus PDFs with forProfile(Balanced); assert jsRemoved>=1 on with_javascript.pdf, EXPECT_TRUE(metadataStripped) on with_metadata.pdf, and zero in the six removal counters on files lacking those elements; do NOT assert metadataStripped on metadata-free PDFs (intent semantics report true there too — left unasserted per ESC-008).
tests.expected_result: Balanced strips JS (jsRemoved>=1) and applies metadata-strip (true on with_metadata.pdf); the six removal counters are 0 elsewhere.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the same four PDFs, when optimized with forProfile(MaxCompression), then >=1 item is removed on each of the four PDFs.
tests.description: Optimize each of the four corpus PDFs with forProfile(MaxCompression); assert total removals >=1 per file.
tests.expected_result: MaxCompression removes >=1 item on each of the four PDFs.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a PDF whose /OpenAction is a non-JS GoTo destination (staged in $TMPDIR, never committed), when optimized under every profile, then the GoTo /OpenAction survives in the output; and given /AA keys present, when optimized with stripJavaScript=true, then /AA is removed with jsRemoved>=1.
tests.description: Stage a $TMPDIR PDF with non-JS GoTo /OpenAction plus /AA keys; optimize under all three profiles; assert GoTo /OpenAction present in every output and /AA removed exactly when stripJavaScript=true.
tests.expected_result: GoTo survives all profiles; /AA removed only under JS-strip.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given --profile balanced plus an explicit --strip-bookmarks override round-tripped through run_optimize CLI parsing semantics (forProfile then explicit flag wins), when optimized, then bookmarks are removed and the result breakdown logs the removal (explicit flag wins over profile default).

tests.expected_result: Explicit flag overrides profile default; removal logged.

tasks.title: Structural writer-options verifier tests (AC-B3)
tasks.description: Create tests/test_structure_writer.cpp verifying object-stream/Flate writer behavior: default output <= --no-dedup --no-flate-recompress output, streamsDeduplicated==0 with defaults (verified current-behavior pin: dedup counting is inert under the ESC-001 isIndirect guard and the reference-shared fixture shares one object by reference, so no distinct duplicate pair exists) and ==0 with --no-dedup on the shared-XObject PDF, and qpdf --check clean on both. Verification only, no product-code change.
acceptance_criteria: Given photo_heavy.pdf (multi-image), when optimized with defaults (deduplicateStreams=true, recompressFlate=true) vs with both disabled, then the default output size is <= the no-opt output size.

Given the transparency/shared-XObject dedup PDF, when optimized with defaults (deduplicateStreams=true) and with --no-dedup semantics (deduplicateStreams=false), then streamsDeduplicated==0 in both runs (verified current-behavior pin: dedup counting is inert under the ESC-001 isIndirect guard, and the reference-shared corpus fixture shares one indirect object by reference so no distinct duplicate pair exists); the aspirational streamsDeduplicated>=1 assertion is deferred to a follow-up phase requiring a product dedup fix plus a distinct-duplicate corpus fixture.
Given both outputs from the comparisons above, when checked with qpdf --check semantics (QPDF::processFile without warnings), then both are clean valid PDFs.
